digest.component_or_area: rebar repository – cross-cutting code, architecture, documentation, and test quality audit
propositions: 87 production modules exceed 500-LOC target; orchestration functions like compute() in next_batch.py and import_tickets() in import_ndjson.py combine multiple responsibilities at high complexity (206+ functions exceed complexity 15), creating maintenance and defect risk despite effective shrink-only ratchet.

Global mypy passes all source, but diagnostic --disallow-untyped-defs found 687 errors; only rebar.graph.* and rebar.grounding.* enforce strictness, leaving broad but shallow type precision across transport boundaries and package interiors.

High-risk architectural seams have bespoke negative controls, but no systemic repository-wide package-dependency contract or DAG enforcement exists; new cross-layer imports rely on review rather than automated detection.

Assignee documentation and quickstart examples teach --assignee alice (README.md:44, docs/user-guide.md:115), but docs/config.md:431 requires Jira-resolvable email/accountId; bare handles are left unassigned, creating user confusion.

Python 3.11 xdist worker exhibits flaky node-down termination in test_opcert_service_app.py::test_matching_guard_is_accepted after ~11.4k passing tests, causing spurious Verified-1 and 8–24 minute rerun latency; identical patch passes unchanged in subsequent run, confirming repeatability defect in CI gate rather than code.
